text:
maria: quick heads-up — after yesterday's queue refactor i'm seeing a regression when we split batches by stage. short prefill p95 jumped on the T4 pool. attaching quick numbers below

sam: ugh — do you have the perf summary or flame traces?

maria: pasted below from the nightly perf run (kernel bench + kv hit tracing). note the weird kernel selection for seq<=8 flows.

perf-bot: perf-run 2026-03-15T03:22Z (suite: split-stage-kernel-probe) finished
```
pool: t4-1
workload: mix-short-prefill-heavy
prefill:
  p50: 12ms
  p95: 64ms
  p99: 118ms
  avg-kv-hit: 0.12
  avg-seq: 7.6
decode:
  p50: 38ms
  p95: 52ms
  p99: 90ms
  avg-kv-hit: 0.65
  avg-seq: 42.1
notes: observed allocator churn and kernel fallback to generic_gemm for short seqs
```

lin: interesting — kernel selection falling back to generic seems tied to our kernel affinity heuristic that now runs after batching assignment. before the refactor we picked kernel based on prefix stats earlier.

rajeev: can we reproduce with a minimal harness? maybe the new queue handshake delays KV warmup so prefill sees low kv-hit and gets routed to an unfriendly kernel.

anya: i dug into traces — it's a timing window: prefill batches are formed with token_budget=2 in the new policy, so many tiny batches not hitting kv cache. small batch + low kv-hit -> weighty kernel chosen.

sam: suggestion: increase token_budget.prefill to 8 for short-prefill flows as an experiment, and adjust queue_policy to prefer mounting prefill until kv warm ratio > 0.3. also add a cheap early kernel probe: if seq<=8 prefer small-seq-optimized kernel.

maria: sounds good. i'm going to flip a canary with these two knobs. deploy command:
```
./deploy -env canary -set phase_scheduler=hybrid -set batches.min_size=2 -set token_budget.prefill=8 -set kernel.affinity.probe=true
```

perf-bot: canary started 2026-03-15T04:01Z

perf-bot: canary metrics after 30m:
```
pool: t4-1
workload: mix-short-prefill-heavy
prefill:
  p50: 11ms
  p95: 29ms
  p99: 58ms
  avg-kv-hit: 0.34
decode:
  p50: 36ms
  p95: 50ms
  p99: 86ms
```

lin: nice improvement on prefill p95. looks like token_budget bump + early kernel probe helped warm kv and avoid generic fallback.

rajeev: we should still check throughput impact. did overall throughput dip because of larger prefill budgets?

maria: throughput flat within 2% on the canary. still need end-to-end perf tests for long sequences and mixed load.

anya: i'll run a kv-warmup microbench and a kernel-selection A/B to quantify misclassification rate before/after. filing a quick eval harness (scripts in /eng-runtime/perf/harnesses).

sam: action items:
- anya: run kernel-selection A/B and kv-warmup bench, post results here
- lin: add a short-circuit in scheduler to prefer small-seq-optimized kernel for seq<=8 if kv-hit < 0.2 (temporary)
- rajeev: validate allocator churn hypothesis with flame traces (compare before/after refactor)
- maria: roll canary to 2 more hosts if tests good

maria: filing perf ticket INF-4123 with the canary numbers and proposed config defaults. will update doc in /eng-runtime/runbook.

sam: one more thought — long term we should avoid hard thresholds. maybe model a lightweight score = alpha*kv_hit + beta*seq_len + gamma*time_in_queue and pick kernel by score. but for now pragmatic knobs are fine.

maria: agreed. low-lift fix first, then move to score-based kernel picker.

perf-bot: note: canary closed 2026-03-15T05:10Z (no regressions in decode path).

maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
